title: Surgical short-flow priority to stop eviction thrashing under microburst floods
text:
Surgical short-flow priority to stop eviction thrashing under microburst floods

description:
Summary: Several customers (two Hosted, one Dedicated, one Private) reported intermittent but severe tail-latency spikes driven by small-request suppression and KV-cache eviction storms during tenant microbursts. Symptom timeline and escalation: on 2026-02-25 we received Pager alerts for three Hosted customers where 95/99th latency jumped 10-40x for short text-completion flows; a Dedicated customer on 2026-02-28 reported repeated failures during batch drain with audit logs showing rapid KV eviction churn. Root cause hypothesis: when a microburst of long-context requests arrives, prefetch and eviction logic aggressively reclaims KV cache and admission windows, which causes in-flight short requests to lose priority, be evicted from warm states, and then be replayed as cold-starts — amplifying load and triggering scheduler admission oscillation. This ticket captures a surgical mitigation: ensure short, latency-sensitive flows get a short-lived "priority immortality" (grace window) that prevents immediate eviction and prefetch preemption during microbursts. The change must be safe across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (vpc/on-prem) and respect tenant isolation and capacity constraints.

comments:
2026-03-02 — Incident triage call: confirmed affected customers share similar load patterns (mix of >8k token inferences plus sub-100 token chat messages). Action: add deterministic logging to admission and eviction paths; baseline dashboards created.
2026-03-04 — Initial experiment: added 50ms 'shortflow grace' in local dev cluster; 95th latency for short requests improved by ~3x under synthetic microburst but overall GPU utilization rose by 4%. Risk noted: naive grace can increase tail for long-context flows if capacity saturates.
2026-03-06 — Design review (ENG + PM + Reliability): decided on adaptive grace that decays if queue/backlog grows beyond threshold and integrates with prefetch telemetry. PM (Jin Park) requested rollout gate and opt-in per-customer flag for Dedicated/Private during initial validation.
2026-03-08 — Implemented admission token for short flows and eviction-hold for KV slots; added backpressure countermeasure to prevent grace-induced convoying. Work in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (WIP).
2026-03-10 — Canary on staging-hosted: 48-hour run shows elimination of short-request cold-start cycles; one Dedicated customer replayed production load in a private cluster and saw reduced 99th by 65%. Observed a pathological case where contiguous long bursts exhaust the grace budget — will add adaptive expiry.
2026-03-11 — Security/ops note: Private deployments must preserve existing KMS/HSM constraints; no key material changes required. Ops (Rohit Gupta) requested explicit metrics for grace-budget consumption for SLO dashboards.
2026-03-12 — Code review feedback from runtime-owners: simplify the admission API surface, add unit tests for eviction hold scenarios, and add a feature flag defaulting to off for existing Dedicated contracts during initial rollout.
Follow-ups: performance tuning (estimate 3 points), add observability for grace window allocation per-tenant (estimate 2 points), and run a weekend canary with two enterprise customers (scheduled 2026-03-18).

resolution_summary:
Partial mitigation implemented: shortflow grace window added with adaptive decay and backpressure checks. Canary results show large improvements for latency-sensitive short requests without significant cost increase in most cases. Remaining work: tighten adaptive expiry heuristics, implement per-customer feature flag for Dedicated/Private, add billing telemetry to track unit-cost impact, and schedule phased rollout with SRE runbook.
